q1.explanationZh: 女孩说妈妈早就安排好周六晚上全家去看望爷爷（visit my grandpa），所以她去不了派对。B 错：派对她去不了；A 错：科幻电影她只是说以后一定要找时间看。

q2.explanationZh: 妈妈问到靴子，男孩说恐怕已经穿不下了，妈妈说“那就换新的吧”（Let’s replace them）。B 错：帐篷可以和 Steve 合用；A 错：手电筒爸爸会借给他。

q3.explanationZh: 表哥现在留着小胡子（上次见他时还没有），以前留长发，现在头发短了（It suits him shorter），所以是短发加小胡子。B 的长发是以前的样子；C 没有胡子也是以前的样子。

q4.explanationZh: 男孩说他把包放在自己房间的衣柜旁边了（next to the wardrobe in my room）。B 错：爸爸嫌包放在客厅桌子旁边碍事，所以挪走了；A 错：前门是他下周打算放包的地方。

q5.explanationZh: 男孩膝盖有伤不能跑，他会在终点线等着给选手拍照（get some good pictures of the runners）。B 错：发水是别人请他做的，但女孩说她会去做；C 错：他今年不能参赛。

q6.explanationZh: 男孩约女孩在图书馆见面，女孩说见完 Lisa 之后会过去找他（I’ll come over to meet you）。C 错：咖啡馆是她和 Lisa 见面的地方；A 错：火车站只是她之后坐车回家的地方。

q7.explanationZh: 比赛原定 11 点，因天气推迟；中午左右（around midday）再做决定，如果那时雨停了就马上开始，所以最早 12 点开始。A 是原定时间；C 是雨不停时的备选时间。

q8.explanationZh: 男孩说本以为游戏会更刺激，其实他对这款游戏不太满意（I wasn’t very impressed），是在承认自己有点失望。A 错：游戏是表哥借给他的，他没花钱；B 错：他没有提出改进建议。

q9.explanationZh: 老师说另外三个人都选了同样的题目，让她换个题目做（she’s asked me to do something else）。B 错：她说自己已经知道一些好网站；C 错：她已经和老师讨论过了。

q10.explanationZh: 男孩说课结束时他打得还可以，但远没有自己希望的那么好（not nearly as well as I’d hoped），说明他对自己的进步感到失望。B 错：他说自己水平还不够，并没有因为没打比赛而生气；C 错：发球很难，但他没说没听懂。

q11.explanationZh: 邻居 Tanya 是教练，她提出可以帮女孩提高棋艺，所以女孩这学期不去俱乐部了。B 错：她说 Tanya 收费不算贵，没说俱乐部会费贵；A 错：她没说自己比别人差。

q12.explanationZh: 男孩以前骑车上学，但住得远，骑车要将近一个小时，很辛苦（it’s nearly an hour on my bike and that’s hard），所以改坐校车。B 错：环保是女孩说的，而且他说骑车更环保；C 错：他的朋友还在骑车，他坐车时喜欢听音乐。

q13.explanationZh: 女孩说穿校服不用想穿什么，可以晚起很多，男孩同意这是个好处（True, that’s a positive thing），所以两人都认为穿校服让上学前的准备更轻松。A 错：男孩认为这是穿校服的原因，女孩不同意；B 错：女孩认为大家穿校服也有很多不同。

q14.explanationZh: Ben 去的是另一家叫 Bridge House 的攀岩中心；Castle Sports Centre 是他提到的城中心那家，并不是他去的。

q15.explanationZh: 约两小时的标准场次就是他们选的，花了 7 英镑 80 便士（seven pounds eighty）。20.70 英镑是月卡，9.50 英镑是三小时场次。

q16.explanationZh: 他自己的运动鞋可以穿，但手表必须放进储物柜（I had to leave my watch in a locker），因为戴着很危险。

q17.explanationZh: 第一次攀岩必须先爬蓝色的墙（I had to go on the blue one）；红色是专家级，紫色是他后来爬的，绿色更难。

q18.explanationZh: 他说回到家时肩膀非常酸痛（my shoulders were really sore）；他以为手会有问题，但手没事。

q19.explanationZh: 地址是 50 号 Wesleigh Road，录音中逐个字母拼出 W-E-S-L-E-I-G-H，注意拼写。

q20.explanationZh: 爸爸很有想象力，常给她讲小熊 Bernie 的冒险故事，她就是这样喜欢上小熊的（That’s how I got into it all）。A 错：Bernie 是爸爸小时候收到的礼物，不是她；C 错：没有提到看别人的收藏。

q21.explanationZh: 她小时候抱着自己的小熊睡觉觉得很安心，现在看到小熊可爱的脸，就会想起那些回忆。B 错：她说收藏也许将来会值钱，但这不是她收藏的原因；A 错：没有提到心情不好的时候。

q22.explanationZh: 她说买到新小熊时，最期待把它加入收藏，看看它和其他小熊放在一起怎么样（adding it to the collection）。A 错：她总是一个人去市场，没说要给熟人看；C 错：没有提到拥有别人没有的东西。

q23.explanationZh: 她认为最重要的是了解你要买的小熊的信息，比如它的历史和有趣的事实（the main thing is to find out information about what you’re getting）。B 错：只买一类小熊是一些收藏者的做法，不是她的建议；C 错：她没有这样说。

q24.explanationZh: 她提醒大家照顾好小熊：阳光直射或清洗会让它们褪色，很多收藏者都吃过这个亏（as so many collectors have found out）。A 错：买到仿制品的情况很少见；C 错：她说大多数收藏者不会把心爱的小熊送人。

q25.explanationZh: 上节目前，她担心观众会觉得她很傻（the programme’s audience thinking I was silly）。A 错：主持人问了很多问题，但那是节目中的事，而且她觉得很好；B 错：她只是说能上很多名人上过的节目很酷。

content.v: Test One. There are four parts to the test. You will hear each part twice. We will now stop for a moment. Please ask any questions now because you must not speak during the test.
Now open your question papers and look at Part One.
For each question, choose the correct answer. Look at question one.
One. What is the girl going to do on Saturday?
I’m really looking forward to Luke’s party on Saturday night. His brother’s band’s playing at it you know. Can we pick you up on the way?
I meant to tell you. My mum’s arranged for us to visit my grandpa that evening – she planned it ages ago. Give Luke a big hug from me, though, won’t you?
I will. Saturday’s busy for lots of people. The school film club’s showing that sci-fi film we were talking about too.
Really? We must get to see that sometime. It sounds great.
Two. What does the boy need to get for his camping trip?
What do we need to organise for your camping trip? That tent of yours is no good.
I know, Mum. I was going to look online and find another one, ’cos it’s full of holes. But Steve’s suggested I share his.
Oh, good idea. And your boots?
Just look at them! I doubt they’ll still fit!
Let’s replace them. And we’ll get you a proper torch. Not that toy thing you’ve got.
Oh, don’t worry about that! Dad’s lending me his one. The light’s amazingly bright.
Three. Who is in the photo?
Do you want to see my holiday photos?
Sure… Wow! Looks like a great place you went to. Is that your cousin? He looks different from how I remember – I’m sure he didn’t have a moustache the last time I saw him.
That was ages ago – he’s grown up a lot since then! He used to have quite long hair as well, down to his shoulders.
I remember now. It suits him shorter. You actually look quite similar now.
A lot of people say that.
Four. Where is the boy’s sports bag?

Hi Mum, it’s Paul. Can you help me? I haven’t got my sports bag at school and we’re playing volleyball later. I know where it is – I put it next to the wardrobe in my room because Dad said it was in the way next to the table in the living room. Anyway you should find it! Please can you bring it over to school? I don’t want to get into trouble! Next week I’ll put it by the front door, so I won’t forget it. Thanks!
Five. What is the boy going to do at the running event?
So have you signed up to enter the fun run?
Oh, didn’t you know? I’ve got a problem with my knee so I’m out of this year’s race. But I’ll be waiting at the finish line ready to get some good pictures of the runners.
For the school magazine?
Yeah. I
was
asked to be one of the people giving out water bottles along the route.
I’m going to do that.
Right – but what I’m doing will make me feel more part of the race somehow.
Six. Where will the friends meet?
I’m going to the library tomorrow afternoon to work on that geography project. Do you want to meet there?

I ought to do something on it too. I’m supposed to see Lisa in the café at the station, though if I don’t stay long with her I could still come. I’m not really sure because she wants to discuss something.
Well, it’s up to you.
I’ll come over to meet you afterwards, but I’ll have to get the train home about four.
I’ll get the train back too.
Seven. What is the earliest time today’s football match could start?

I’m afraid today’s football match will be postponed until a bit later. The original start time was eleven this morning but due to the very bad weather conditions, we’re going to see what’s happening in the next hour or so, around midday, and make a decision then. If it’s stopped raining heavily at that time, we can start immediately. If not, maybe we can begin playing at one. If we can’t do that, we’ll have to cancel.
That is the end of Part One.
Now look at Part Two. For each question, choose the correct answer.
Eight. You will hear two friends talking about a computer game.
Have you played that new computer game yet –
Critters 2
Not yet. Is it any good?

It’s definitely a lot better than the first version that came out … better sound effects, for a start. And the colours are really cool. But … I don’t know … I kind of thought it’d be a bit more exciting. I guess what I’m saying is that I wasn’t very impressed. Oh well … at least I can’t say it cost a lot.
Oh? Why’s that then?
Well my cousin lent it to me. That’s why!
Just as well.
Nine. You will hear two students talking about a history project for school.
I’ve been thinking about that history project we’ve got to do. How about you?

Yeah, I discussed what I’m going to do with our teacher yesterday. She said that three other people all wanted to do the same subject as me. Probably because there are so many new articles about it online. Anyway, she’s asked me to do something else.
That’s a shame.
Oh, it’s OK. She’s given me loads of ideas so I’m not that worried.
I’ll tell you where to look online for ideas if you like.
Thanks, I already know some good ones so I’m fine actually.
Ten. You will hear a boy talking to his friend about a tennis lesson.
How was your tennis lesson today?

OK. My instructor spent most of it showing me how to serve the ball to start the game off. It was difficult! You have to throw the ball up in the air and hit it hard as it falls. By the end of the lesson, I was doing OK, though not nearly as well as I’d hoped.
So, have you had any long games?
No, I’ve only had a few lessons so far. I’m just not really good enough yet. Maybe one day.
Eleven. You will hear two friends talking about a chess club.
I haven’t seen you at chess club. Everyone’s been asking about you, hoping you’re coming back.

Yeah. They’re lovely, but I’m not coming this term. I was talking to the woman next door, Tanya, about chess – she’s a coach. And she suggested she could help me with my game. The price she’s charging isn’t too bad so…
But some of the people at the club give really good advice.
It’s not that they don’t. I just felt I needed an expert to train me, even if I have to pay for it. Who knows, I might come back!
Twelve. You will hear two friends talking about travelling to school.
I see you’re taking the bus to school nowadays. That’s good ’cause cars cause so much pollution.

True. Though actually, I always used to come by bike, which is even better because there’s no pollution from that. But because I live quite far away, it’s nearly an hour on my bike and that’s hard, especially in the winter.
Really? Well at least now you can meet up with all your mates before school. Like me. We chat the whole way.
Oh well, Tim and Mike are still cycling, actually, but I enjoy just sitting listening to music on my phone.
Thirteen. You will hear two students talking about the uniform at their school.
I hate having to wear school uniform. Nobody can show their individual style.
If you look at other people in uniform, you’ll see loads of differences. The way they do their tie, or their shirt, or what socks they wear…
I’d prefer to choose what I wear.
But now I don’t have to think about that, so I can get up much later than before.
True, that’s a positive thing. An extra half an hour!
And everyone says we look so smart.
Really? I think that’s why we’re expected to wear uniforms.
I’m not so sure that’s the main reason.
That is the end of Part Two.
Now look at Part Three.
For each question, write the correct answer in the gap. Write one or two words or a number or a date or a time. Look at questions 14 to 19 now. You have 20 seconds.
You will hear a boy called Ben giving a class talk about an indoor climbing centre he went to.

Hi, I’m Ben and I’d like to tell you about a climbing centre. If you’re into climbing, I expect you know the Castle Sports Centre in the middle of town. My visit was to another climbing centre called Bridge House. It’s by the river and it’s really good.

My dad took me there at the weekend and now we’re thinking about becoming members. There are different prices. A month’s membership is twenty pounds seventy, or you can book a standard session, lasting a couple of hours, which is what we did. That was seven pounds eighty. For nine pounds fifty you can get a session of three hours.

All equipment’s provided, including special climbing shoes. I wanted to wear my own trainers and they let me, but I had to leave my watch in a locker. They said it’s dangerous to have things like that on. Every climber gets given a helmet to wear too.

The walls have different colours depending on your climbing level. I can’t wait to get to the expert one. That’s red. I had to go on the blue one because it was my first time. That’s the one for people who are new to it, but I soon got onto the purple one. And there’s a green one after that. They get more and more difficult.

It’s easy to hurt yourself if you don’t follow the instructors. Having strong arms helps. Personally, my shoulders were really sore by the time I got home. I thought I’d have problems with my hands, but they were fine.
So where is this place? The address is number 50, Wesleigh Road, that’s spelt W-E-S-L-E-I-G-H. It’s easy to find and it’s got a covered area to leave your bike if you want to cycle there.
Now, any questions?
That is the end of Part Three.
Now look at Part Four. For each question, choose the correct answer.
Look at questions 20 to 25 now. You have 45 seconds.
You will hear an interview with a girl called Sofia, who collects toy bears.
Sofia, you have over a hundred toy bears in your collection. How did you become interested in bears?

Because of a bear called Bernie! He belonged to my dad – he was given Bernie as a kid. Dad has a great imagination, and he’d entertain me with Bernie’s adventures. That’s how I got into it all. Mum has an old bear, too, and their two toys sit together on a shelf at home.
Why do you like collecting bears so much?

It’s cos when I was a kid I felt safe with my own toy bear in my arms, falling asleep. I don’t hug the bears I’ve got now, but those memories come back when I look at their cute faces. My collection might become valuable in the future – who knows? It’d be nice but it’s not why I do it.
How do you find bears to buy?

I go to markets. I go alone – friends can put you off if they don’t like something. Then you might not buy the bear you’ve seen and another collector buys it instead! When I get a new bear, I really look forward to adding it to the collection and seeing how it fits in.
Any advice for people who want to collect bears?

Not really, but I know some collectors often just buy one kind and become experts on them – like antique ones or famous brands. I guess the main thing is to find out information about what you’re getting – its history, interesting facts. It could be one of a particular kind, or completely individual.
What mistakes can you make when collecting bears?

If you’re buying a bear that’s supposed to be made by a designer, make sure it isn’t a copy. That’d be a waste of money, but it’s pretty rare. And take care of your bears – they’ll lose their bright colours in direct sunlight or if you wash them – as so many collectors have found out. And avoid giving a favourite bear away even if a friend tries to persuade you! Most collectors are unlikely to do that.
You recently appeared on a TV programme with your bears!

Yes. I wasn’t that comfortable with the idea of the programme’s audience thinking I was silly. That’d be embarrassing. I wanted to explain why as a teenager I was still collecting toys! Actually, the presenters were really interested in what I do and asked me loads of things. It was cool being on a show I’d seen so many celebrities on.
That is the end of Part Four.
You now have six minutes to write your answers on the answer sheet.
You have one more minute.
That is the end of the test.
